country.comment: The study was conducted in the municipality of Juiz de Fora, Minas Gerais, Brazil.
country.where_found: PDF p. 1, Title & Abstract; PDF p. 2, Section 2; PDF p. 3, Section 3.1

effect_estimate.comment: Purely qualitative study; coder reliability metrics (agreement > 80% and Krippendorff's alpha > 0.8) are methodological checks rather than empirical effect estimates.
effect_estimate.value: Qualitative — no numeric effect estimate reported. National Law No. 11.445/2007, Juiz de Fora Municipal Law No. 14.290/2020, the 2022 Municipal Water and Sanitation Plan, and CESAMA's 2021 Bylaws define water and sewage services around occupied households and building connections, creating legal ambiguity and excluding public spaces from utility mandates. Combined with weak cross-sectoral coordination across municipal departments, lack of accountability, public procurement delays, heritage/environmental permitting blocks (e.g., a 2-year closure and CONPUR embargo of the Halfeld Park toilet renovation; >1-year startup delay and withheld SESMAUR authorization for the Alma Lavada container toilet), and political discontinuity, public toilets and drinking fountains remain scarce or closed, leaving informal street vendors reliant on improvised arrangements ('sevirologia') with formal shops or paid private toilets (~US$0.50 per use).
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract; PDF pp. 3–8, Sections 3.1–3.3 & Section 4 (Table 1)

mechanism_certainty.comment: Primary qualitative study (CASP ceiling = 2) that directly observes and documents through statutory/bylaw analysis, site observations, and interviews with municipal managers and street vendors how household-bounded legal mandates, inter-departmental fragmentation, heritage/environmental permitting blocks, and procurement rules restrict public water and toilet provision.

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines household/building-connection legal scope exclusions (service_area), land-ownership and heritage/urban planning obstacles (property, planning), private toilet user charges and municipal vendor license fees (fees), procurement/permitting hurdles and >1-year implementation/repair delays (procedural_steps, delay), administrative/managerial discretion including operating without inter-departmental authorization (discretion), and severe cross-sectoral fragmentation and political discontinuity (institutional_fragmentation, political_coordination).
mechanism_flags.value: ELIGIBILITY, BURDEN, DISCRETION_ACCOMMODATION, service_area, property, planning, fees, procedural_steps, delay, discretion, institutional_fragmentation, political_coordination

outcome_flags.comment: Analyzes street vendors' access to public drinking water fountains and toilets, private toilet fees (~US$0.50/use), hygiene/cleanliness/water pressure and disability accessibility, facility closures and restricted operating hours (9 a.m.–6 p.m.), and >1–2 year delays in opening/renovating and repairing public facilities.
outcome_flags.value: water_access, sanitation_access, affordability, service_quality, service_continuity, delay

publication_year.comment: Published in Utilities Policy Volume 97 (2025) 102051; available online 11 September 2025.
publication_year.where_found: PDF p. 1, journal header and article history footer

risk_of_bias_tool.comment: Primary qualitative study using focused ethnography, semi-structured interviews, and qualitative content analysis; appraised with the CASP Qualitative Checklist per RISK_OF_BIAS.md §1.

sample_size.comment: Non-probabilistic snowball sampling conducted up to theoretical saturation within an estimated downtown population of 459 informal workers (123 fixed street vending spots plus itinerant vendors).
sample_size.value: 30 semi-structured interviews (24 informal street vendors and 6 municipal public managers) in Juiz de Fora

study_design.comment: Focused ethnography conducted between 2021 and 2023 combining field observations, legal/policy document analysis, and snowball-sampled semi-structured interviews analyzed via Schreier (2012) qualitative content analysis.
study_design.value: Qualitative focused ethnography with semi-structured interviews and qualitative content analysis
study_design.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract; PDF pp. 2–3, Section 2
